extracted.intended_audience: lobbying registrants, in-house lobbyists, lobbying firms, and compliance officers required to file LDA disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for compliance with the Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA) reporting and registration requirements, including LD‑1/LD‑2 quarterly activity reports and LD‑203 semiannual contribution reports, filing deadlines, thresholds, and use of the online filing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly activity reporting requirement (LD-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995, as amended, requires all active registrants to file quarterly activity reports with the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives and Secretary of the U.S. Senate (LD-2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports cover fixed quarterly periods (First Quarter: Jan 1–Mar 31; Second: Apr 1–Jun 30; Third: Jul 1–Sep 30; Fourth: Oct 1–Dec 31). Specific due dates are provided (typically April 20, July 20, October 20, January 20) and the guidance notes that if a deadline falls on a weekend or holiday the report is due the following business day. Filers should use the current LD-2 form and follow the Clerk/Senate instructions for filing and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semi-annual contribution reporting requirement (LD-203)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Honest Leadership and Open Government Act of 2007 requires active lobbying registrants and individual lobbyists to file a semi-annual report of certain contributions (LD-203) along with certification regarding gift and travel rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mid-Year (Jan 1–Jun 30) and Year-End (Jul 1–Dec 31) contribution reports are due July 30 and January 30 respectively (or the next business day). Registrants and each of their lobbyists who were active for all or part of the reporting period must file separate reports. Filers must sign the report and certify that they understand House and Senate gift and travel rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of contribution reports (LD-203) — types of contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contribution reports must detail certain FECA contributions, honorary contributions, Presidential Inaugural Committee contributions, Presidential Library contributions and certain payments for event costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system provides a pre-populated contribution form for each filer. Filers must ensure all applicable categories (FECA, honorary, inaugural committee, presidential library, event cost payments) are reported for the relevant period and that separate entries are filed for registrant and each active lobbyist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration thresholds and exemptions (who must register)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration thresholds determine when a lobbying firm or an organization employing in-house lobbyists must register under the LDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As effective Jan 1, 2025: a lobbying firm whose total income for matters related to lobbying activities on behalf of a client does not exceed or is not expected to exceed $3,500 in the quarterly period is not required to register with respect to that client; an organization employing in-house lobbyists is not required to register if its total expenses in connection with lobbying activities do not exceed and are not expected to exceed $16,000 in the quarterly period. The $3,000/$13,000/$14,000 historical values are noted in prior revisions. Section 4(a)(3) provides that registration threshold dollar amounts be adjusted every four years based upon changes in the Consumer Price Index; the next adjustment will be made Jan 1, 2029.

rubrics_metrics.name: JACK Act disclosure requirement (Justice Against Corruption on K Street Act of 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any listed lobbyist who was convicted in a Federal or State court of specified offenses, registrations (LD-1) and quarterly reports (LD-2) filed after Jan 3, 2019 must include the date of conviction and a description of the offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified offenses include bribery, extortion, embezzlement, illegal kickback, tax evasion, fraud, conflict of interest, making a false statement, perjury, or money laundering. If the amended forms are not yet available in the filing system but the statutory timeline requires filing, filers should file the registration or quarterly report and then amend the filing to include the required JACK Act information once the forms/systems are updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines schedule and business-day rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance publishes the calendar of statutory filing deadlines for quarterly activity reports and contribution reports and explains the business-day adjustment rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly Activity Reports: First Quarter due April 20 (covers Jan 1–Mar 31), Second Quarter due July 20 (Apr 1–Jun 30), Third Quarter due October 20 (Jul 1–Sep 30), Fourth Quarter due January 20 (Oct 1–Dec 31). Contribution Reports: Mid-Year due July 30 (Jan 1–Jun 30), Year-End due January 30 (Jul 1–Dec 31). If a deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, the report is due the following business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online filing system transition and technical filing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing has transitioned to an online LD filing system (LDWebBeta / LDWeb) and older IBM forms were discontinued; filers must use the web-based system for LD-1, LD-2, and LD-203 submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the online system at https://lda.congress.gov/LDWebBeta (or provided links). Log in using your Senate ID and password (same ID/password used for other lobbying disclosure forms). The system supports selecting filing year and report type, automated retrieval of lobbyist ID numbers/passwords, and a single-button submission to file to both House and Senate. Training resources (online tutorials, user manual, troubleshooting guide, FAQs, DVDs mailed to registrants) and help contacts are provided. IBM forms will no longer be accepted after specified cut-off dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: System features: pre-population, account access, and lobbyist verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The online filing system provides pre-populated forms and account features tied to existing registrations and requires lobbyist identity verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features include automated retrieval of lobbyist ID numbers and passwords, pre-populated forms containing appropriate ID numbers, names, and contact information; the ability to save filings and retrieve them for amendment; a process where the employer must verify the registered lobbyist name before an account is created for each employee; and each lobbyist must create a unique password prior to access. Communications regarding filing and account status are automated and sent to the address on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing amendment process and interim guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on filing amendments and actions to take when form changes/systems are not yet updated to reflect statutory changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filings can be saved, retrieved, appended, and amended after filing using the online system. Where statutory timelines require filing before amended forms are available (e.g., JACK Act fields), filers should file on time using current forms and then amend filings to include newly required information when the system/form updates are released. Notices address the impact of filing an amended LD-1 or LD-2 on the duty to file an LD-203 and provide clarifications where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance revision topics and section updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clerk and Secretary periodically revise written LDA guidance; revisions enumerate which guidance sections have been updated and summarize substantive changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions cited include updates to Section 3 (Definitions), Section 4 (Lobbying Registration), Section 5 (Special Registration Circumstances), Section 6 (Quarterly Reporting of Lobbying Activities), Section 7 (Semiannual Reporting of Certain Contributions), Section 8 (Termination of a Lobbyist/Registrant), and Section 10 (Public Availability). Each revision announcement links to the revised guidance (HTML/PDF) and highlights substantive additions (e.g., listing affiliates, disclosure of covered officials, JACK Act additions, updated registration thresholds).
